entities.summary: Alfred Charles Kinsey was an American sexologist, biologist, and professor of entomology and zoology who, in 1947, founded the Institute for Sex Research at Indiana University, now known as the Kinsey Institute for Research in Sex, Gender, and Reproduction. He is best known for writing Sexual Behavior in the Human Male (1948) and Sexual Behavior in the Human Female (1953), also known as the Kinsey Reports, as well as for the Kinsey scale. Kinsey's research on human sexuality, foundational to the field of sexology, provoked controversy in the 1940s and 1950s, and has continued to provoke controversy decades after his death.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kinsey's research on human sexuality laid the groundwork for modern sexology and challenged societal norms around sex, influencing subsequent generations of researchers and social reformers. His work remains a foundational aspect of contemporary discussions on sex education, LGBTQ+ rights, and sexual health.
